semantic/architecture/separate-decisions.note: Rule: keep business logic pure and push I/O to the edges; business-rule code must not hide I/O. Same rule, framed as functional core / imperative shell.

semantic/architecture/thin-entry-points.note: Directory-scoped rule for HTTP handlers: parse/validate request shape, call services, respond. Same shape the policy describes.

semantic/design/explicit-dependencies.note: Avoid globals and pass dependencies through function parameters, with exemptions for constants and immutable config. Covers the global/singleton half of the policy; says nothing about constructing collaborators internally or reading env vars.

semantic/design/no-flag-parameters.note: A bool that is a behavior switch or a bare true/false argument becomes an enum or named-field struct; a bool that reads as a predicate stays. Rust-flavored wording of the same rule.

semantic/design/preserve-error-context.note: Preserve the original exception when translating errors (exception chaining) and do not replace a useful exception with a generic message. Does not say to name the failed operation beyond "adding context".

semantic/design/single-responsibility.note: One reason to change per class, methods do one thing, do not mix I/O, business logic, and presentation. Trimmed: the bullets on one type per file and on comment-driven extraction were dropped as separate rules.

semantic/encapsulation/minimal-public-su.note: Do not export types or functions unless they need to be shared across components.

semantic/encapsulation/protect-internal-.note: One bullet from the repo's "Do Not" list: do not expose mutable state via getters. Covers returning internal mutable state; says nothing about storing callers' mutable objects.

semantic/maintainability/no-duplicated-k.note: Extract duplicated logic that represents the same concept, but not look-alike code. Same rule and the same exemption as the policy.

semantic/naming/intent-revealing-names.note: Name things for what they mean, not how they are built. Same rule; one example and no list of generic placeholder names.

semantic/organization/cohesive-modules.note: No utils/helpers grab-bag files; one concern per file. Also includes a ~300-line size heuristic from the same bullet.

semantic/readability/comments-explain-wh.note: Comment only for context the code cannot show (constraint, invariant, quirk, tradeoff); do not narrate or repeat code. Says nothing about comments that contradict the code.

semantic/readability/consistent-abstract.note: One bullet from a Clean Code checklist: one level of abstraction per function, do not mix high-level policy with low-level details.

semantic/readability/explain-magic-value.note: Extract meaningful or recurring values into named const/enum, keep self-explanatory one-off values inline, use constants for spec values such as HTTP statuses.

semantic/testing/descriptive-test-names.note: Test names should be descriptive and include the symbol and the criteria, with two examples.

semantic/testing/test-behavior-not-imple.note: Test observable outcomes, not how a function was called; asserting call shape and call counts is called out. The next bullet (mocks are a smell) was not included because it is a separate, stricter rule.

_omitted.semantic/naming/names-match-behavior: No permissively licensed AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/copilot-instructions/.cursorrules rule found that says a function name must not understate or misdescribe its side effects. Searched for name/side-effect/misleading-name/getter/"name suggests"/"name promises"/command-query-separation phrasings; the matches were either in unlicensed or copyleft repos (varianter/tid: no license; lincolnq/avalanche: AGPL-3.0; Habitat-Thinking/ai-literacy-superpowers: NOASSERTION; morfidon/ai-agents: no license), or were about something else (CQS rules that never mention names; librick/ic1101 asks for the opposite direction, names that promise more than the body does).
